questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An element with molar mass $2.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ forms a cubic unit cell with edge length of 405 pm . If its density is $2.7 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$, the number of atoms present in one unit cell of it is (Given : $\left.\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}=6.023 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
The number of atoms present in one unit of element can be calculated by $\begin{aligned} & n=\frac{N_a \times \rho}{M \times V} \\ & n=\text { Number of atom per unit } \\ & \rho=\text { density of element } \\ & N_2=6.023 \times 10^{23} \\ & M=\text { Molar mass of element }=2.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \\ & V=\text { Volume of unit cell } \\ & V=a^3=\left(405 \times 10^{-12}\right)^3=6.685 \times 10^{-29} \\ & n=\frac{6.023 \times 10^{23} \times 2.7 \times 10^3}{2.7 \times 10^{-2} \times 6.685 \times 10^{-29}} \\ & n=4 \end{aligned}$
Number of atom per unit cell of the element is approximately 4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the correct statement about the crystal defects in solids,
options: Frenkel defect is favoured when the difference between sizes of cation and anion is very small
Frenkel defect is not a dislocation effect
Schottky defects have no effect on physical properties of solids
Trapping of electrons in lattice leads to the formation of F-centres
questions.solution:
Trapping of electrons in Lattice leads to the formation of F - centres.
1- Frenkel defect is favoured when the difference between size of cation and anion is larger.
2- Frenkel defect is also called dislocation defect.
3- Schottky defect have effect on phyṣical properties o? solids. It decreases the density of the substance.

questions.q: The molecular formula of a compound is $\mathrm{AB}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$. Atoms of O form ccp lattice. Atoms of A (cation) occupy $\frac{1}{8}$ th of tetrahedral voids. Atoms of B (cation) occupy a fraction of octahedral voids. What is the fraction of vacant octahedral voids?
questions.solution:
No. of tetrahedral voids is twice the no. of atoms. No of octahedral voids is same as the no. of atoms. oxygen at ccp = 1
A occupy $\frac{1}{8}$ of tetrahedral voids i.e. $\frac{1}{8} \times 2=\frac{1}{4}$
Atoms of B (Cation) occupy octahedral voids i.e $\frac{1}{2} \times 1=\frac{1}{2}$
Fraction of vacant octahedral voids $=1-\frac{1}{2}=1 / 2$

No. of $Y$ atoms per unit cell $=\left[\left(8 \times \frac{1}{8}\right) \times 8\right]-1=7\Rightarrow$ Empirical formula $=\mathrm{X}_8 \mathrm{Y}_7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct option for axial distances and axial angles for hexagonal crystal system is
questions.solution: Hexagonal crystal system comprises four axes. The three axes are all contained within a single plane (called the basal plane) and are at 120°. They intersect each other at an angle of sixty degrees. The fourth axis intersects other axes at right angles. The edges at the base have equal length and the edges present at right angles have different length form the edges at the base. Hence, axial distances and axial angles are a=b≠c, α=β=90°, γ=120°

questions.solution:
Angle between (100) and (110) planes of fcc lattice is
$\cos \phi=\frac{h_1 h_2+k_1 k_2+l_1 l_2}{\sqrt{h_1^2+k_1^2+l_1^2 \sqrt{h_2^2+k_2^2+l_2^2}}}\cos \phi=\frac{(1 \times 1)+(0 \times 1)+(0 \times 0)}{\sqrt{(1)^2+(0)^2+(0)^2} \sqrt{(1)^2+(1)^2+(0)^2}}\cos \phi=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow \phi=45^{\circ}$

questions.q:
In a bcc lattice having the edge length of $200 \mathrm{pm}$, the cation has the radius of $70 \mathrm{pm}$.
The radius ratio of $\frac{r^{+}}{r^{-}}$is
(Given, $\sqrt{2}=1.4, \sqrt{3}=1.7$ and $\sqrt{6}=2.4$ )
questions.solution:
$\because$ For bcc lattice, radius ratio for $r^{+} / r^{-}$is 0.7 , i.e. radius ratio of cation by anion ranges from 0.732 to 1.0. Also, for bcc $r^{-}$ions are at corners, Thus,
$4 \times r^{-}=\sqrt{3} a \quad(\because \sqrt{3} a=1.7 \times 200)$
(where, $a=$ edge length)
and $\quad 4 \times r^{-}=1.7 \times 200r^{-}=\frac{1.7 \times 200}{4}=85 \mathrm{pm}\therefore \quad \frac{r^{+}}{r^{-}}=\frac{70}{85}=0.82$, which is close to 0.7.

questions.q: Copper crystallises in cсp arrangement and accepted value of metal ion radius was found to be $1.14 Å$. Calculate the density of copper in grams per cubic centimetre. (Atomic weight of copper is $64, N_A=6 \times 10^{23}$ )
questions.solution:
Given, copper crystallises in ccp manner radius $=1.41 Å=141 \mathrm{pm}$
Atomic weight of copper $=64$
Avogadro's number $=6 \times 10^{23}$, Density $=$ ?
$\rho=\frac{Z \times M}{a^3 \times N_a}$
Here, edge length of unit cell can be calculate as
$\begin{aligned}
& r=\frac{a}{2 \sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow a=r \times 2 \sqrt{2} \\
& a=141 \times 2 \times 1.414 \\
& a=398.74 \text { pm or } 398.74 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~cm}
\end{aligned}$
Volume of unit cell $=\left(398.74 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~cm}\right)^3$
For
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { сср }=2=4, \\
& N_a=6.0 \times 10^{23} \\
& f=\frac{4 \times 64}{\left(398.74 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~cm}\right)^3 \times 6.0 \times 10^{23}} \\
& f=6.73 \approx 6.67
\end{aligned}$
Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many of the following compounds show ferrimagnetism?

\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4 ; \mathrm{MgFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 ; \mathrm{NiFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 ; \mathrm{MnO} ; \mathrm{CrO}_2
questions.solution:
In ferrimagnetic substances, the magnetic moments of the domains are alligned in parallel and antiparallel directions in unequal number. The net magnetic moment is small. Thus, these are weakly attracted by magnetic field than ferromagnetic substances and these also lose ferrimagnetism on heating and become paramagnetic. e.g. $\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4$ and ferrites like $\mathrm{ZnFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4, \mathrm{MgFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ and $\mathrm{NiFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ etc.
$\uparrow \uparrow \downarrow \uparrow \uparrow \downarrow$
Ferrimagnetism
Among the given options, we have 3 compounds (i.e. $\mathrm{Fe}_3 \mathrm{O}_4, \mathrm{MgFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ and $\mathrm{NiFe}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ ) that show ferrimagnetism.
Hence, option (3) is the correct answer.

questions.q: A compound can crystallise in two forms $\alpha$ and $\beta$ which are fcc and bcc, respectively. The $\alpha$-form has side length of $2 \mathrm{pm}$ and the $\beta$-form has side length of $4 \mathrm{pm}$. The ratio of their density $\frac{\rho_\alpha}{\rho_\beta}$ i
questions.solution:
Density $\left(\rho_\alpha\right)$ for $\alpha$-form $=\frac{M Z_1}{N_0\left(a_1\right)^3}$
and density $\left(\rho_\beta\right)$ for $\beta$-from $=\frac{M Z_2}{N_0\left(a_2\right)^3}$
Given, 
side length $\left(a_1\right)$ for $(\alpha)=2 \mathrm{pm}$ 
side length $\left(a_2\right)$ for $(\beta)=4 \mathrm{pm}$ 
where, $M=$ molar-mass
$N_0=$ Avagadro number
$Z_1$ and $Z_2=$ number of particles in $\alpha$ and $\beta$ form. $a_1$ and $a_2$ are side lengths.
Here, $Z_1=4, Z_2=2, a_1=2, a_2=4\therefore \quad \frac{\rho_\alpha}{\rho_\beta}=\frac{M Z_1 / N_0\left(a_1\right)^3}{M Z_2 / N_0\left(a_2\right)^3}=\frac{Z_1 \times\left(a_2\right)^3}{Z_2 \times\left(a_1\right)^3}\frac{\rho_\alpha}{\rho_\beta}=\frac{4 \times(4)^3}{2 \times(2)^3}=\frac{256}{16}=16$

questions.solution:
Given, the radius ratio of anion to cation $=10: 9.3\therefore$ The radius ratio of cation to anion $=9.3: 10=0.93$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The cubic unit cell of a metal (molar mass $=63.55 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ ) has an edge length of $362 \mathrm{pm}$. Its density is $8.92 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$. The type of unit cell is
questions.solution:
Density, $d=\frac{M Z}{N_0 a^3}$
where, $Z=$ number of atoms in unit cell
$\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad Z & =\frac{d N_0 a^3}{M} \\
& =\frac{8.92 \times 6.023 \times 10^{23} \times\left(362 \times 10^{-10}\right)^3}{63.55} \\
& =4.0
\end{aligned}$
Thus, metal has face centred unit cell.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If an element having atomic number 96 crystallises in cubic lattice with a density of $10.3 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$ and the edge length of $314 \mathrm{pm}$ then, the structure of solid is
questions.solution:
Given, Density of element $(d)=10.3 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$
Edge length $(a)=314 \mathrm{pm}$
Avogadro number $\left(N_A\right)=6.02 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Molar mass $(M)=247 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}[\because Z=96$, having molar mass 247 , i.e. cesium (Cs) $]\because \quad d=\frac{Z \times M}{a^3 \times N_A}$
where, $Z=$ number of lattice points in a unit cell
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad \quad \quad Z=\frac{d \times a^3 \times N_A}{M} \\ & Z=\frac{10.3 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3} \times(314)^3 \times 10^{-30} \mathrm{~cm} \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}{247 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}} \\ & Z=0.78 \approx 1\end{aligned}$
Thus, the structure of solid is simple cubic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Assertion (A) White tin is an example of tetragonal system.Reasoning (R) For a tetragonal system $a=b=c$ and $\alpha=\beta=\gamma \neq 90^{\circ}$. The correct answer is
options: (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of $(\mathrm{A})$.
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is true but (R) is not true.
(A) is not true but (R) is true.
questions.solution:
White tin, an allotropic form of tin is an example of tetragonal system and for tetragonal system, one side is not equal to other two while all the angles are equal, ie, $a=b \neq c$ and $\alpha=\beta=\gamma=90^{\circ}$.
Hence, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is not.
